requirement: The review prompt MUST direct the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question instead. When the reviewer splits a committed requirement, the prompt MUST direct it to keep the requirement's full name on the core obligation, to name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and to list every new name.
rationale:
The requirement sets two prompt-content obligations. (1) The prompt must tell the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question. (2) When the reviewer splits a requirement, the prompt must tell it to keep the full name on the core obligation, name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and list every new name.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_never_renames_and_names_split_parts]` is marked `{test}`. It takes the prompt text between "**Mechanical changes:**" and "**Design questions:**" using `review_prompt_between`. That helper collapses whitespace and panics if either delimiter is missing. The test then uses `assert_text`, which asserts `contains` for each phrase:
- "Never rename or move a committed requirement; if its name is wrong, raise it as a design question" covers obligation 1.
- "When you split one, keep its full name on the core obligation and name the parts `<name>.<part>`" covers keeping the full name and the part naming.
- "List every new name" covers listing every new name.

The prompt asset `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md` has this wording in its requirement group review section. Dropping or altering any directive would make the test fail. Scoping the check to the mechanical-changes section also confirms the directives sit where the prompt sets out the reviewer's changes. I found no untested obligation, wrong expectation, or marking gap.
